strengths: Pioneering mechanistic interpretability study in diffusion transformers (DiTs), extending circuit analysis from autoregressive language models to text-to-image generative diffusion dynamics.
Methodological innovation with 'Attention Synopsis', which systematically and tractably summarizes cross-attention patterns across millions of maps over layers, heads, and diffusion sampling steps.

Comprehensive causal verification: the identified two-stage circuit in RTE-DiT (spatial relation head L2H8 and object generation head L4H3) is thoroughly validated through targeted attention ablations, QK circuit decomposition, and causal activation injection.

Insightful contrast between RTE-DiT and T5-DiT, demonstrating how pretrained text encoder representations fundamentally alter internal generative circuits (modular cross-attention vs. in-embedding contextual fusion), backed by variance partitioning and vector arithmetic interventions.
Provides a compelling mechanistic explanation for the prompt sensitivity and spatial reasoning failures often observed in modern text-to-image models.
weaknesses: Experiments are conducted exclusively on a synthetic toy domain (3 2D shapes, 2 colors, 128x128 resolution). While controlled environments are essential for mechanistic interpretability, evidence of whether these specific circuit patterns scale or persist in open-domain, photorealistic models (e.g., SD3, PixArt-alpha, Flux) remains unverified.

The scope of text encoders analyzed in depth is limited to T5-XXL and synthetic RTE. The paper does not investigate CLIP encoders or multimodal/dual-encoder configurations commonly employed in production diffusion architectures.
Some formatting and referencing choices in the main paper could be refined; for example, Table 2 and Figure 10 are frequently cited in the main narrative but appear exclusively in the appendix.

strengths: Principled mechanistic interpretability approach to generative diffusion transformers: The paper tackles a recognized failure mode in text-to-image models (spatial relation composition) through a rigorous reverse-engineering framework, dissecting attention heads, QK/VO circuits, and representation geometry.

Methodological contribution with Attention Synopsis: The proposed aggregation methodology reduces the high-dimensional attention tensor across sampling steps, layers, heads, and token categories into interpretable synopses, effectively overcoming the complexity of analyzing iterative diffusion trajectories.

Rigorous causal validation: Beyond observational attention heatmaps, the authors validate their hypotheses with causal interventions, including targeted head ablations (L2H8 and L4H3), cross-head activation injection (injecting L2H8 VO output into L4H3 input), and factorized vector arithmetic in the T5 embedding space.

Insightful comparison between text conditioning schemes: The contrast between random token embeddings (RTE) and pretrained T5 embeddings reveals how frozen contextual encoders shift the computational burden—T5 compresses relation and object semantics into single token representations, whereas RTE forces the DiT backbone to synthesize its own modular two-stage spatial tagging and attribute binding circuits.
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on a synthetic toy domain: The models are trained entirely from scratch on a highly restricted synthetic dataset (three geometric shapes, two colors, plain background, 128x128 resolution). It remains unproven whether the clean, localized circuits (e.g., single heads dominating spatial tagging and shape generation) persist in large-scale diffusion models trained on natural, complex web data.

Lack of empirical verification on existing open-source DiT checkpoints: While the paper references models like PixArt-alpha and SD3, it does not evaluate whether similar relational circuits or contextual fusion dynamics can be observed or probed in off-the-shelf pretrained foundation models.

Prompt diversity and confounding in T5 sensitivity: The dataset uses very simple prompt templates with only 10,000 samples. The vulnerability of T5-DiT to minor prompt perturbations (e.g., adding 'the') may largely stem from severe overfitting to the restricted synthetic training prompt distribution rather than being an intrinsic limitation of contextual text encoders.

Unexplored occlusion relations: Although Section B.1 describes generating occlusion pairs ('in front of', 'behind'), the mechanistic analysis focuses almost exclusively on 2D directional relations, leaving the depth/occlusion mechanism unexamined.

strengths: Compelling mechanistic interpretability approach applied to spatial relation generation in Diffusion Transformers (DiTs), targeting a well-known failure mode of current text-to-image models.

The proposed 'Attention Synopsis' method effectively reduces the high-dimensional cross-attention space across diffusion steps, layers, and heads into interpretable category-to-category interaction patterns, providing a reusable tool for analyzing DiTs.

Thorough causal validation: the identified circuits are verified through head-specific ablations, causal activation injection (injecting L2H8 VO output into L4H3 image positional inputs to trigger selective attention), and semantic vector arithmetic on T5 token embeddings.

Illuminating comparison between random token embeddings with positional encodings (RTE) and pretrained contextual embeddings (T5): clearly demonstrates that the nature of the text encoder fundamentally alters the circuit mechanism used by the DiT (explicit two-stage modular circuit vs. contextual information fusion shortcut), offering a concrete explanation for prompt sensitivity.
weaknesses: Evaluation is restricted to a synthetic toy dataset consisting of simple 2D geometric shapes (circles, squares, triangles) on flat backgrounds at 128x128 resolution; validating whether these specific circuit behaviors persist in full-scale open-domain models (e.g., full PixArt-alpha, SD3, FLUX) remains an open challenge.

While the paper contrasts T5 and RTE, modern frontier models frequently use dual or different encoders (such as CLIP / OpenCLIP combinations or decoder LLMs like LLaMA/Gemma); exploring or discussing these would strengthen the generality of the conclusions.

The paper lacks an empirical demonstration of how the discovered circuit mechanisms can be harnessed into concrete remedies (e.g., an inference-time guidance or training objective) to enhance spatial relation composition in real-world settings.

Presentation and layout organization could be improved: several figures and tables cited prominently in the main text (e.g., Table 2 and Figure 10) are located in the appendix, disrupting the flow of reading.

strengths: Compelling mechanistic interpretability study targeting a critical and well-known failure mode in Diffusion Transformers (DiTs): compositional multi-object spatial relation generation.

Methodological innovation with 'Attention Synopsis' and a fast, weight-space QK screening technique that detects spatial-gradient-inducing cross-attention heads without requiring full image generation runs.

Rigorous causal validation combining head-specific attention ablations, direct VO-output injection into positional embeddings (demonstrating two-stage tagging and routing in RTE-DiT), and targeted vector arithmetic in the contextual embedding space (demonstrating steerable spatial relations in T5-DiT).

Insightful explanation of prompt brittleness: demonstrates that contextual text encoders (e.g., T5) fuse spatial relation semantics into object tokens, causing minor lexical perturbations (like inserting filler words like 'the') to distort the spatial relation direction and collapse generation accuracy.
Extensive experimental support across multiple model scales (nano to base), text encoders (RTE, T5, CLIP), and preliminary verification on a full-scale pre-trained model (PixArt-Sigma).
weaknesses: The primary experimental framework relies on a highly simplified toy dataset (three 2D geometric shapes, two colors, 128x128 resolution). While controlled environments are standard in mechanistic interpretability, findings may not fully capture the complexity of open-domain, multi-layered natural scenes.

The analysis on the pre-trained real-world model (PixArt-Sigma in Section 5 / Appendix A.10) is relatively preliminary; it demonstrates head screening and token masking on a small set of prompts but lacks the depth of causal activation patching and circuit surgery performed on the synthetic models.

The paper is primarily diagnostic and does not validate concrete architectural or training remedies (e.g., explicit decoupling objectives or prompt-conditioning constraints) to mitigate the identified contextual fusion brittleness in full-scale DiTs.

strengths: Pioneering mechanistic interpretability study in Diffusion Transformers (DiTs): While mechanistic circuit analysis has gained substantial traction in language models, rigorous mechanistic studies of text-to-image diffusion models remain scarce. This work offers a fresh and timely perspective on spatial relational reasoning in generative models.

Rigorous causal validation: Rather than relying solely on observational attention visualizations, the authors support their claims with rigorous causal interventions, including specific cross-attention head ablations, VO activation patching between heads, and direct vector arithmetic in the contextual embedding space.

Insightful mechanistic distinction between text encoders: The paper provides a clear and compelling explanation for how text representations dictate internal DiT mechanisms: RTE induces a modular two-stage circuit (spatial gradient tagging followed by attribute binding), whereas contextual encoders (T5, CLIP) fuse relational signals into noun tokens, explaining why contextual models are uniquely brittle to subtle prompt perturbations (e.g., adding filler words like 'the').

Novel and scalable analysis methodology: The proposed 'Attention Synopsis' and 'Weight-Space Head Screening' techniques provide efficient ways to localize functionally relevant cross-attention heads directly from model weights and positional encodings without running full sampling trajectories.
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on a synthetic toy domain: The core models are trained and analyzed on a highly simplified 2D synthetic dataset consisting of three basic geometric shapes, two colors, and eight discrete relations on a uniform background. While toy setups are standard in mechanistic interpretability, real-world generative distributions feature high visual diversity, complex attribute interactions, and realistic scenes that may exhibit more diffuse circuits.

Limited validation on pre-trained foundation models: The transferability analysis to full pre-trained models (PixArt-Sigma in Appendix A.10) is preliminary and hampered by the fact that the baseline model exhibits low out-of-the-box spatial accuracy (only 8 of 30 object pairs showed non-trivial performance), leaving open questions about how robustly these findings scale to commercial or web-scale T2I models.

Inclusion of occlusion relations in dataset generation without detailed circuit analysis: The dataset creation method (Appendix B.1) details 3D/occlusion relations ('in front', 'behind'), yet the mechanistic analysis primarily focuses on 2D directional ramp templates, leaving the depth composition circuit underexplored.

Organization of material between main text and appendix: Key supporting experiments—such as evaluations on CLIP-DiT, robustness sweeps, and pretrained model analysis—are relegated to the appendix, while some sections of the main text could be streamlined to accommodate these broader evaluations.

strengths: Compelling mechanistic interpretability study: The paper provides a clear, fine-grained circuit explanation of how Diffusion Transformers process and render spatial relations between multiple objects, uncovering a stark difference between non-contextual (RTE) and contextual (T5/CLIP) text encoders.

Methodological innovation in DiT analysis: The introduction of 'Attention Synopsis' and the training-free 'Weight-Space Head Screening' provides efficient, scalable tools for tracing cross-attention communication and hypothesis-driven head identification without running millions of expensive sampling runs.

Rigorous causal validation: The claims are rigorously backed by causal interventions, including head-specific attention knockouts, feature injection across sequential heads (L2H8 to L4H3), and linear vector arithmetic in the contextual token embedding space to systematically steer spatial placement.

Insights into real-world T2I brittleness: The analysis offers a grounded explanation for why models conditioned on pretrained LLMs/CLIP fail at spatial reasoning, demonstrating that information fusion in contextual tokens creates extreme sensitivity to lexical and syntactic perturbations (e.g., adding filler words).

Thorough empirical analysis and scaling checks: Experiments span multiple model sizes (DiT-B down to DiT-nano), different text encoders (RTE with/without pos, T5, CLIP), and include preliminary transfer experiments to pre-trained PixArt-Sigma.
weaknesses: Toy dataset constraints: The primary mechanistic analysis is conducted on a highly stylized synthetic domain of 2D geometric shapes on uniform backgrounds. While appropriate for controlled circuit analysis, it remains an open question how cleanly these modular circuits persist in complex natural scenes with multi-object occlusions, textures, and depth.

Limited validation on large-scale pre-trained models: The analysis on pre-trained PixArt-Sigma (Appendix A.10) is constrained because the model itself exhibits very low baseline spatial accuracy (only 8 of 30 object pairs showed non-trivial success), meaning the full circuit tracing pipeline could not be validated with the same completeness as in the synthetic setup.

Lack of an algorithmic mitigation: While the paper thoroughly characterizes why T5-conditioned DiTs fail under prompt perturbations, it stops short of evaluating proposed architectural or training remedies (e.g., separate relation-routing tokens or modified cross-attention layers) to resolve the observed brittleness.
